title: Scalable GPU tenancy bands and fallthrough contract experiment
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run an experiment to validate a banded GPU tenancy model that combines reserved tenancy bands, a metered fallthrough pool, and an explicit 'preemptible lane' for cost-sensitive customers. Goal: surface a commercially viable SKU framework that simplifies enterprise contracting while preserving predictable throughput and graceful capacity fallback for production workloads.
background: Current offerings are focused on fixed reserved commits + burst credits. Customers ask for simpler negotiation constructs for multi-team enterprises: a set of guaranteed throughput bands with automatic fallthrough to a lower-cost metered pool and an option to accept preemptible capacity for non-critical workloads. Legal and security teams also require a standardized addendum for SLAs and an updated security questionnaire response template for dedicated contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 tenancy bands (Baseline / Elevated / Peak) with clear throughput/GPU equivalents and per-band pricing
Design fallback policy that routes overflow to metered pool or preemptible lane based on tenant preferences and runtime SLOs
Contracting template (term sheet + SLA addendum) drafted and reviewed by Legal/Product Ops
Pilot signed with 2 existing mid-market customers and engineering confirms integration with Dedicated autoscaler prototype
Measure unit economics: realized cost per 1M tokens and latency P50/P90 under overflow scenarios
pricing_matrix: Baseline Band: reserved 1-4 GPU-equivalent lanes, guaranteed 95% availability, price = $X per vGPU-hour (negotiable at scale)
Elevated Band: reserved 5-16 GPU-equivalent lanes, guaranteed 97% availability, price = Baseline * 1.35, includes 10% burst credit buffer
Peak Band: reserved 17+ GPU-equivalent lanes, guaranteed 99% availability, price = Baseline * 1.7, includes priority routing and dedicated KV cache sizing
Fallthrough Metered Pool: pay-as-you-go price per vGPU-minute, lower priority; automated fallback with configurable throttles
Preemptible Lane (optional): 30-50% discounted price, best-effort capacity, suitable for batch/async workloads; preemption notice 5 minutes
experiment_design: Pilot cohort: 2 customers (one AI-native startup, one mid-market SaaS) with heterogeneous traffic patterns
Duration: 8 weeks with three phases: onboarding (2w), steady-state (4w), stress/overflow tests (2w)
Engineering: instrument autoscaler hooks to simulate metered fallthrough and record routing decisions
Finance: capture invoicing delta between committed vs realized spend and reconciliation friction points
Legal: validate SLA wording and map to existing incident / credit mechanics
metrics: Throughput yield: tokens/second per reserved vGPU across bands
Latency SLOs: P50/P90/P99 under reserved and fallthrough scenarios
Unit cost: $ per 1M tokens realized during pilot vs modelled baseline
Fallback frequency: percentage of requests routed to metered pool or preemptible lane
Customer qualitative score: onboarding friction and perceived predictability (NPS-like)
risks: Customers misunderstand fallthrough semantics and expect unlimited burst at reserved price
Preemptible lane could cause customer data residency or audit concerns if not isolated
Engineering complexity to guarantee KV cache isolation at band boundaries
Legal pushback on SLA credit caps when combining reserved and metered components
